title: Sheila Guys and Louella: the marriage prophecy
summary: Louella announced they would marry in front of Sheila Guys; a year later she repeated it and Pete Johnson warned her.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So, the meantime, when we went to have dinner, I run into Little Bo (?) and Sheila Guys (?). They was in the restaurant, too.
"I'm doin'...I'm fine. What're you doin' down here?"
Say, "Well, I came down here to work with Sheila Guys. She got us a job at the club she's workin' at.
I say, "Well, how nice!" So we had a good time together.

So I said, "Well, now, I want you to meet a friend of mine." So Sheila Guys said, "I don't wanna meet no woman o' yours." I say, "She no woman o' mine." I said, "She's a friend. At least, you can say 'hello'." So we finally got together. Sheila Guys went on like she and me was so tight so git it, give Louella whattya idea...I don't know where she got it from. So's she pulled up. She says, "well, uh, I got news for you." She says, "Me and Joe Turner gonna get married." So I said, "Whhu-u-u-u-utt?" Says, "Yeah." Says, "We gonna get married." I say, "Not me! I ain't never been married in my life. I don't think I want to get married." She say, "It'll come around to ya. It'll grow on ya." So I just thought she's makin' a joke. So, finally, about a year later, I'd went off to Indianapolis...run aroun' all over the country...so I came back to Chicago. I went back to the same hotel where I met her at. So, by that time I'd got...I knowed the fellow that run the hotel. Boy, he was after her himself, so he wouldn't give me no room. Say, "I ain't got no room, Joe." I say, "Louelly still live here?" "Yass, she still lives here." I say, "Okay, then, I'll just speak to her afore I go." So I knocked on her door. Louelly was asleep. Say, "Who is that?" Said, "Joe Turner! Who you think it is, knockin' on your door this time o' mornin'?" She say, "Wait a minute." She got up, come to the door, say,
So I say, "Okay," so me and Pete Johnson went on in. So we sit aroun' an' we went out and had breakfast an' we was talkin' and rappin' back an' forth.
An' she said, "Y'know, you don't forget what I tol' ya." Just outa the clear, blue sky, she said, "We gonna get married. I tol' ya that."
So Pete Johnson said, "Man, you don't wanna marry Joe Turner. Joe Turner's wild as a deer. Ain't nothin' you can do with him."
So I say, "How you know? How you know, I might like it, y'know."
So I just let it go like that. I said, "Well, there ain't no need of me talkin' 'bout that no more. I ain't got it on my mind where I'm gonna marry nobody..." to myself, y'know.
